symbols.name: \(P_n\)
symbols.space: joint laws of observed and potential variables

symbols.name: \(f_{d,n,x,k}\)
symbols.role: conditional potential-outcome marginal used in the perfect-compliance reduction

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{PT}}\)
symbols.def: The completed result \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) proves that the exact selected-complier partial-transport capacities are \(\Pi_+w_n\) and that the sharp benefit set is the closed interval \(\Theta_{I,n}=[N_{L,n}/M_n,N_{U,n}/M_n]\), with both endpoints attained by compatible latent couplings.
symbols.role: imported exact-capacity and closed sharp-endpoint mapping

symbols.name: \(\widehat q^d_{n,z,x,k}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat q^d_{n,z,x,k}=N^d_{n,z,x,k}/\max\{N_{n,x,z},1\}\); hence every empty empirical \((x,z)\) cell is assigned conditional selected-outcome proportions equal to zero.

symbols.name: \(\widehat w_n\)
symbols.def: \((\widehat w_n)_x=\widehat p_{n,x}(\widehat\ell_{n,x,0},\ldots,\widehat\ell_{n,x,K-1},\widehat h_{n,x,0},\ldots,\widehat h_{n,x,K-1})^{\prime}\), stacked over \(x\in\mathcal X\). This formula is used without screening on every finite sample.

symbols.name: \(\widehat v_n\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat v_n=\Pi_+\widehat w_n\), including coordinates arising from empty empirical cells.

symbols.name: \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}=\widehat M_n\) if \(\widehat M_n>0\), and \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}=1\) if \(\widehat M_n=0\).
symbols.role: fixed positive fallback for the plug-in quotient denominator

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_{L,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{L,n}=\min\{1,\max\{0,\widehat N_{L,n}/\widehat M_n^{\dagger}\}\}\). In particular, it equals zero when \(\widehat M_n=0\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\theta_{U,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\widehat\theta_{U,n}=\min\{1,\max\{0,\widehat N_{U,n}/\widehat M_n^{\dagger}\}\}\). In particular, it equals zero when \(\widehat M_n=0\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\)
symbols.def: Stack over \((x,k)\) the components \[\widehat\psi^{\ell}_{n,x,k}(O_{ni})=(\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=x\}-\widehat p_{n,x})\widehat\ell_{n,x,k}+\widehat p_{n,x}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=x\}Z_{ni}}{\max\{N_{n,x,1}/n,1/n\}}\{\mathbf 1\{D_{ni}=1,S_{ni}=1,Y_{ni}=k\}-\widehat q^1_{n,1,x,k}\}-\widehat p_{n,x}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=x\}(1-Z_{ni})}{\max\{N_{n,x,0}/n,1/n\}}\{\mathbf 1\{D_{ni}=1,S_{ni}=1,Y_{ni}=k\}-\widehat q^1_{n,0,x,k}\},\] and \[\widehat\psi^h_{n,x,k}(O_{ni})=(\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=x\}-\widehat p_{n,x})\widehat h_{n,x,k}+\widehat p_{n,x}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=x\}(1-Z_{ni})}{\max\{N_{n,x,0}/n,1/n\}}\{\mathbf 1\{D_{ni}=0,S_{ni}=1,Y_{ni}=k\}-\widehat q^0_{n,0,x,k}\}-\widehat p_{n,x}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_{ni}=x\}Z_{ni}}{\max\{N_{n,x,1}/n,1/n\}}\{\mathbf 1\{D_{ni}=0,S_{ni}=1,Y_{ni}=k\}-\widehat q^0_{n,1,x,k}\}.\] If an empirical \((x,z)\) cell is empty, its indicator and residual contribution are exactly zero, so every component is finite on every sample.

symbols.name: \(\Sigma_{w,n}\)
symbols.def: \(\Sigma_{w,n}=E_{P_n}[\psi_{w,n}(O_{n1})\psi_{w,n}(O_{n1})^{\prime}]\) on the nonredundant raw-capacity contrast coordinates.

symbols.name: \(\Sigma_{c,n}\)
symbols.def: The covariance of the influence vector for the stacked conditional contrasts \((\ell_{n,x,k},h_{n,x,k})_{x,k}\) under total-sample \(\sqrt n\) scaling.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R\)
symbols.def: The Cartesian family of compatible orthant masks, lower zero or cut branches, survivor-minimum branches, upper cut branches, and upper mass-cap branches generated explicitly by \(\Pi_+\), \(m\), \(b_L\), and \(b_U\).

symbols.name: \(A^L_r\)
symbols.def: For each cell, let \(D\) be the diagonal zero-one mask recorded by \(r\). The zero branch contributes \(0\); a cut \(t\) with gap branch \(\gamma\in\{0,1\}\) contributes \(D[(\mathbf 1\{k\le t\}-\gamma\mathbf 1_K)_{k=0}^{K-1},(-\mathbf 1\{k\le t\}+\gamma\mathbf 1_K)_{k=0}^{K-1}]^{\prime}\). Stack these cell vectors over \(x\).

symbols.name: \(A^U_r\)
symbols.def: For each cell mask \(D\), an upper cut \(t\) contributes \(D[(\mathbf 1\{k<t\})_{k=0}^{K-1},(\mathbf 1\{k>t\})_{k=0}^{K-1}]^{\prime}\); a mass-cap branch contributes either \(D[(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime},0^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) or \(D[0^{\prime},(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) according to the selected survivor minimum. Stack over \(x\).

symbols.name: \(B_r\)
symbols.def: For each cell mask \(D\), the lower-total survivor branch contributes \(D[(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime},0^{\prime}]^{\prime}\) and the upper-total branch contributes \(D[0^{\prime},(\mathbf 1_K)^{\prime}]^{\prime}\); \(B_r\) stacks the branch selected by \(r\) over \(x\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\)
symbols.def: Construct \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) explicitly from \(\widehat w_n\): for coordinate \(j\), retain only the release mask if \(\widehat w_{n,j}>a_n\), only the binding mask if \(\widehat w_{n,j}<-a_n\), and both masks otherwise; for the gap and survivor-minimum comparisons retain both signs when the absolute difference of their affine inputs is at most \(a_n\), and otherwise retain the empirical sign; retain every lower zero or cut branch within \(a_n\) of the empirical maximum and every upper cut or mass-cap branch within \(a_n\) of the empirical minimum. The retained set consists of every compatible Cartesian combination of these choices.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\)
symbols.def: The population face family formed by applying the same branch-slack rules as \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) with tolerance \(a_n/4\) and deterministic localization constants.

symbols.name: \(\xi_i\)
symbols.def: Independent standard Gaussian multipliers, independent of the data.

symbols.name: \(G_n^*\)
symbols.def: \(G_n^*=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\widehat\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\), with the totalized influence vector used even if some empirical \((X,Z)\) cell is empty.

symbols.name: \(c_{n,1-\alpha}\)
symbols.def: \(c_{n,1-\alpha}=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:P_{\xi}[\max_{r\in\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}}\{\widehat g^L_{n,r}{}^{\prime}G_n^*,\widehat g^U_{n,r}{}^{\prime}G_n^*\}\le t\mid O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}]\ge1-\alpha\}\). The retained Cartesian family is nonempty on every sample, so this generalized-inverse quantile is defined even when \(G_n^*\) is degenerate.

symbols.name: \(\mathrm{CI}_n\)
symbols.def: \(\mathrm{CI}_n=[\max\{0,\widehat\theta_{L,n}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n\},\min\{1,\max\{0,\widehat\theta_{U,n}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n\}\}]\); if the displayed lower endpoint exceeds the upper endpoint under an off-support finite-sample realization, set \(\mathrm{CI}_n=\{0\}\).
symbols.role: confidence interval for the entire sharp identified set

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_n\)
symbols.role: event that every required empirical covariate-instrument cell is nonempty

symbols.name: \(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}\)
symbols.def: For the diagnostic support \(\mathcal X=\{1,2\}\), set \(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,1}=1/4\) and \(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,2}=1/\sqrt n\), with \(n\ge16\).
symbols.role: cellwise always-selected-complier mass in the boundary diagnostic

symbols.name: \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\)
symbols.def: For every \(x\in\{1,2\}\), \(z\in\{0,1\}\), and \(r\in\{0,1,2\}\), the table has exactly four rows \[(x,z,1,1,1,1,r,r;1/48),\quad(x,z,0,0,1,1,r,r;1/48),\] \[(x,z,0,1,1,1,r,r;m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/12),\quad(x,z,0,1,0,0,r,r;(1/2-m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x})/12).\] Each tuple lists \((X_{ni},Z_{ni},D_{ni}(0),D_{ni}(1),S_{ni}(0),S_{ni}(1),Y_{ni}(0),Y_{ni}(1);\text{probability})\), and every tuple not displayed has probability zero.

symbols.name: \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\)
symbols.def: The law supported exactly on \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\), with observed variables generated by \(D_{ni}=D_{ni}(Z_{ni})\), \(S_{ni}=S_{ni}(D_{ni})\), and \(Y_{ni}=Y_{ni}(D_{ni})\) when \(S_{ni}=1\).

symbols.name: \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m)\)
symbols.role: conditional raw-capacity contrast covariance block implied by the atom table

symbols.name: \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\)
symbols.def: Adapt automatic generalized-moment selection to the finite projection, gap, survivor-minimum, cut, and mass-cap slacks by studentizing each slack with its empirical covariance and calibrating a data-dependent near-face threshold through the common multiplier process.
symbols.role: method handle for tuning-free face retention

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P_n\).
The potential selection and outcome variables depend on instrument assignment only through \(D_{ni}(z)\).
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\sigma_{n,x}\{S_{ni}(1)-S_{ni}(0)\}\ge0\) almost surely conditional on \(C_{ni}=1\) and \(X_{ni}=x\).
Every eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) on the nonredundant conditional-contrast space lies in \([\underline\lambda,\overline\lambda]\).
Every population-inactive coordinate, gap, survivor-minimum, lower-cut, upper-cut, and mass-cap branch has slack at least \(\delta_0\).

standard.name: uniform slack separation for moment selection

definitions.name: fixed-support survivor-complier class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}: J\ge2,\ K\ge3,\ \text{and for every }n\text{ the member properties in }\texttt{ass:iid-row}\text{ through }\texttt{ass:raw-covariance-band}\text{ hold}\}\).

definitions.name: sharp survivor-complier benefit interval
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{I,n}=[N_{L,n}/M_n,N_{U,n}/M_n]\), where each numerator uses the displayed finite lower-cut or upper-cut-and-mass-cap formulas after \(\Pi_+\).

definitions.name: imported exact partial-transport identification mapping
definitions.construction: Use the established theorem \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{PT}}\) from \(\texttt{CausalSmithPartialTransport2026}\): map the observed raw capacities \(w_n\) to \(\Pi_+w_n\), then to \(M_n\), \(N_{L,n}\), and \(N_{U,n}\), and hence to the exact closed sharp set \(\Theta_{I,n}=[N_{L,n}/M_n,N_{U,n}/M_n]\).

definitions.name: finite-sample empirical-cell totalization
definitions.construction: For every finite sample, compute \(N_{n,x}\), \(N_{n,x,z}\), and \(N^d_{n,z,x,k}\); use \(\max\{N_{n,x},1\}\) and \(\max\{N_{n,x,z},1\}\) in conditional empirical proportions, assigning zero numerators and hence zero conditional proportions to empty cells. Form \(\widehat w_n\), \(\widehat v_n\), \(\widehat M_n\), \(\widehat N_{L,n}\), and \(\widehat N_{U,n}\) from those proportions, and use the fixed fallback \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}=1\) when \(\widehat M_n=0\). In the estimated influence vector use \(\max\{N_{n,x,z}/n,1/n\}\) for every empirical joint-cell denominator. These conventions determine the retained faces, multiplier process, generalized-inverse critical value, and \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) on all samples.

definitions.name: unscreened nonnegative-projection plug-in
definitions.construction: Compute the totalized conditional proportions \(\widehat q^d_{n,z,x,k}\), form \((\widehat w_n)_x=\widehat p_{n,x}(\widehat\ell_{n,x,0},\ldots,\widehat\ell_{n,x,K-1},\widehat h_{n,x,0},\ldots,\widehat h_{n,x,K-1})^{\prime}\), apply \(\widehat v_n=\Pi_+\widehat w_n\) coordinatewise without deleting any cell, evaluate every displayed cut and mass branch, and divide by \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}\) to form \((\widehat\theta_{L,n},\widehat\theta_{U,n})\).

definitions.name: least-favourable survivor-support face envelope
definitions.construction: Retain \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) at tolerance \(a_n\), evaluate the explicit quotient gradients \(\widehat g^L_{n,r}\) and \(\widehat g^U_{n,r}\), and take their common conditional multiplier maximum; no latent linear program is solved.

definitions.name: unpadded whole-set confidence interval
definitions.construction: \(\mathrm{CI}_n=[\max\{0,\widehat\theta_{L,n}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n\},\min\{1,\max\{0,\widehat\theta_{U,n}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n\}\}]\), using the totalized endpoint estimators and generalized-inverse conditional quantile; on the off-support event that the displayed lower endpoint exceeds the displayed upper endpoint, set \(\mathrm{CI}_n=\{0\}\).

definitions.name: complete changing-support atom law
definitions.construction: For each \(x\in\{1,2\}\), \(z\in\{0,1\}\), and \(r\in\{0,1,2\}\), assign the four atom probabilities in \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\), assign zero to every other tuple, and generate the observed variables by consistency; this constructs \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\).

definitions.name: studentized automatic-retention handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) to construct a data-dependent tolerance for every explicit branch slack from studentized generalized-moment-selection scores and the common multiplier process, while retaining all faces selected by the resulting simultaneous rule.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the event that every empirical \((X,Z)\) cell is nonempty. Uniformly over \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal P\), \[\sup_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}P_n(\mathcal E_n^c)\le 2J(1-p_0\varepsilon)^n\longrightarrow0.\] On \(\mathcal E_n\), every denominator fallback in \(\widehat e_{n,x}\), \(\widehat q^d_{n,z,x,k}\), and \(\widehat\psi_{w,n}\) is inactive, and the totalized \(\widehat w_n\), \(\widehat v_n\), endpoint estimators, retained face family, multiplier process, critical value, and \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) equal their ordinary empirical-cell counterparts. Consequently totalization changes any coverage probability by at most \(2J(1-p_0\varepsilon)^n\) and does not alter the limit in \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\).
statements.justification: This proposition closes the finite-sample domain of every empirical and multiplier object without changing the uniform first-order experiment.
statements.gap: Asymptotic cell-probability arguments often leave conditional empirical ratios undefined on empty cells; the explicit exponential bound makes the proposed whole-set procedure a genuine finite-sample map.
statements.consumer: It permits software for sparse Job Corps covariate cells to return a deterministic interval on every dataset while preserving the theorem's uniform coverage guarantee.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \((P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal P\), with probability tending to one, \[\max\{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_{L,n}-\theta_{L,n}),\sqrt n(\theta_{U,n}-\widehat\theta_{U,n})\}\le\max_{r\in\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)}\{g^L_{n,r}{}^{\prime}n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni}),g^U_{n,r}{}^{\prime}n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{w,n}(O_{ni})\}+o_{P_n}(1),\] where \(\mathcal R_n^0(P_n)\) is contained in \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) with probability tending to one.
statements.justification: This is the deterministic bridge from a drifting nonsmooth quotient to a finite Gaussian maximum.
statements.gap: Directional-delta results linearize at one law; they do not dominate both signed endpoint secants along paths that cross projection and survivor-support faces.
statements.consumer: It supplies a reusable verification device for exact finite capacity bounds without solving a bootstrap linear program.

statements.statement: Conditional on the established exact-capacity and closed sharp-endpoint mapping \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{PT}}\), for fixed \(J\), fixed \(K\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), the procedure defined on every finite sample by \(\texttt{def:finite-sample-totalization}\) satisfies \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(P_n)\in\mathcal P}P_n\{\Theta_{I,n}\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The infimum includes arrays with simultaneous endpoint ties, zero raw capacities, arbitrary rates of cellwise survivor-mass disappearance, and zero survivor-mass gaps; \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) contains no deterministic padding beyond its conditional multiplier critical value.
statements.justification: This is the headline uniform inference result at the joint boundary geometry actually generated by survivor-benefit bounds.
statements.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen document undercoverage of the ordinary \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap at boundary laws and use a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) remedy; they do not prove uniform, no-padding, whole-identified-set coverage for the projected survivor-complier quotient with changing support. Fang and Santos and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker do not supply that field-level result either.
statements.consumer: A Job Corps analysis can report an honest confidence interval for the full sharp range of the probability that an always-employed complier moves to a higher wage category.

statements.statement: Under \(\texttt{ass:oracle-separation}\), the retained empirical family equals the population active projection-and-branch family with probability tending to one, and the conditional critical value \(c_{n,1-\alpha}\) differs by \(o_{P_n}(1)\) from the oracle face-envelope critical value that knows this family.
statements.justification: The theorem shows that uniform protection has no first-order critical-value cost on regular separated faces.
statements.gap: Generalized moment selection handles slack inequalities, but not simultaneous support release and nested ratio branches in this explicit capacity map.
statements.consumer: Applied users obtain ordinary smooth-face precision when Job Corps cells are well separated while retaining protection when they are not.

statements.statement: If each cell survivor mass is positive and every endpoint has a unique separated projection, minimum, and cut branch, then \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) is first-order equivalent to the ordinary joint Gaussian delta-method interval based on the two active quotient gradients.
statements.justification: This is the required regular-case reduction and guards against paying for nonexistent ties.
statements.gap: It recovers the familiar smooth endpoint limit as a corollary rather than imposing smoothness on the main class.
statements.consumer: It lets standard software and influence-function calculations validate the new implementation on well-separated empirical designs.

statements.statement: Under perfect compliance, \(D_{ni}(0)=0\) and \(D_{ni}(1)=1\), and universal selection, \(S_{ni}(0)=S_{ni}(1)=1\), one has \(\ell_{n,x,k}=f_{1,n,x,k}\), \(h_{n,x,k}=f_{0,n,x,k}\), \(w_{n,x}=p_{n,x}(f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}\), and \(M_n=1\). Consequently \(\Theta_{I,n}=[\sum_x p_{n,x}b_L((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime}),\sum_x p_{n,x}b_U((f_{1,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{1,n,x,K-1},f_{0,n,x,0},\ldots,f_{0,n,x,K-1})^{\prime})]\), the covariate-stratified ordinary sharp ordinal-benefit bounds; without covariate stratification these are the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta bounds.
statements.justification: This reduction checks that the selected-complier capacity formulas collapse to the established ordinal-benefit geometry when compliance and observability cease to be latent.
statements.gap: Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta establish the ordinary ordinal-benefit bounds; this proposition is a required reduction, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It gives implementers an exact benchmark for validating the capacity and min-cut code against standard two-arm ordinal data.

statements.statement: Set \(J=2\), \(K=3\), and \(\sigma_{n,1}=\sigma_{n,2}=1\). For \(n\ge16\), the atom table \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) sums to one and induces \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) with \(p_{n,1}=p_{n,2}=e_{n,1}=e_{n,2}=1/2\). Its only nonzero selected observed cells, for every \(x\in\{1,2\}\) and \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\), are \[q^1_{n,0,x,k}=1/12,\quad q^1_{n,1,x,k}=1/12+m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3,\quad q^0_{n,1,x,k}=1/12,\quad q^0_{n,0,x,k}=1/12+m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3.\] Hence \(\ell_{n,x,k}=h_{n,x,k}=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3\), \(m((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/2\), \(b_L((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=0\), and \(b_U((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3\). Thus \(M_n=1/8+1/(2\sqrt n)\), \(N_{L,n}=0\), \(N_{U,n}=1/12+1/(3\sqrt n)\), and \(\Theta_{I,n}=[0,2/3]\). The two conditional-contrast covariance blocks are \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,1})\) and \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,2})\); the eigenvalues of \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m)\) are \((2+4m)/3\) with multiplicity four, \((2+4m-4m^2)/3\), and \((1-4m^2)/3\). Consequently every eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) lies in \([1/4,1]\), and \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\in\mathcal P\) for constants satisfying \(p_0\le1/2\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\), \(m_0\le1/8\), \(\underline\lambda\le1/4\), and \(\overline\lambda\ge1\).
statements.justification: The complete atom calculation shows that changing survivor support and simultaneous cut ties coexist with ordinary instrument overlap and a uniformly nondegenerate raw first stage.
statements.gap: This is an internal legality and stress-test result for the main uniform theorem, not a claim that a named published implementation fails.
statements.consumer: It gives method developers a reproducible boundary benchmark for testing Job Corps-style implementations without relying on an underdetermined latent law.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), can one construct a fully data-dependent studentized face-retention rule whose common-multiplier confidence interval preserves the uniform whole-set coverage conclusion of \(\texttt{thm:uniform-face-envelope}\) over \(\mathcal P\) and remains first-order equivalent to the oracle face envelope under \(\texttt{ass:oracle-separation}\), without requiring the analyst to specify a deterministic sequence \(a_n\)?
statements.justification: Automatic studentized retention would remove the only deterministic tuning sequence from the otherwise explicit finite-face procedure.
statements.gap: Andrews and Barwick calibrate automatic moment selection for moment inequalities, but do not cover the linked projection, numerator-cut, survivor-minimum, and denominator faces of this quotient map.
statements.consumer: A Job Corps analysis could use a reproducible default calibration while retaining protection against changing wage-cut and survivor-support faces.

sampling_model.design: Row-wise i.i.d. sampling from a conditional-IV triangular array with fixed finite \(J\) and \(K\).
sampling_model.units: Observed units are \(O_{ni}=(X_{ni},Z_{ni},D_{ni},S_{ni},S_{ni}Y_{ni})\); potential variables obey the stated IV and principal-stratum restrictions.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary instrument \(Z_{ni}\), binary received treatment \(D_{ni}\), no defiers, and exclusion.
sampling_model.overlap: Covariate-cell and instrument propensities are uniformly bounded away from zero, and only aggregate survivor-complier mass is bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Every empirical conditional proportion uses the explicit count-denominator fallback in \(\texttt{def:finite-sample-totalization}\). Raw capacities are unscreened, projected onto the nonnegative orthant, and coupled to one Gaussian multiplier draw through the totalized finite-dimensional influence vector; the plug-in quotient uses \(\widehat M_n^{\dagger}=1\) only when its empirical denominator is zero.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp symbolic probability-of-benefit bounds are paired with a study of \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws and a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap remedy.
Sharp lower and upper bounds on the probability that treatment is beneficial for an ordinal outcome are determined by the two treatment-arm marginal distributions.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian first-stage limit requires full differentiability, and estimated directional derivatives provide an alternative.
Selected-complier mean-bound estimators are jointly root-\(n\) normal and semiparametrically efficient under trimming regularity, margin, and overlap conditions.
Adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian critical values yield inference for intersection bounds.
Estimated directional derivatives and localized optimizer sets yield uniform inference for optimized value-function statistics.
Randomly perturbed linear programs yield uniform coverage of an outer set and exact coverage on a further outer target.

tldr: The completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem supplies the exact selected-complier capacities and closed sharp benefit endpoints as an established input. Every empirical conditional proportion, projected capacity, influence component, multiplier quantile, and confidence interval is totalized on all finite samples by an explicit count-denominator convention, whose activation probability vanishes uniformly. Because the projected piecewise linear-fractional map can change active cuts and survivor support at the \(n^{-1/2}\) scale, the procedure keeps every empirically near-active projection, gap, survivor-minimum, cut, and mass-cap face and calibrates the largest of the two signed endpoint errors with one conditional multiplier process. The main theorem gives uniform root-\(n\) coverage of the entire sharp interval without deterministic padding, oracle equivalence recovers ordinary precision on separated faces, the formulas reduce to ordinary ordinal-benefit bounds under perfect compliance and universal selection, and a complete finite atom table supplies a legal changing-support stress test.

project_justification.gap: Existing ordinal-benefit work supplies sharp symbolic bounds and studies ordinary-bootstrap boundary undercoverage with a conservative subsampling remedy, but does not prove uniform no-padding coverage of the entire projected survivor-complier quotient interval. Generic nonsmooth and intersection-bound methods do not directly handle the interacting orthant projection, changing cell support, nested min-cut branches, two signed endpoints, and common denominator.
project_justification.niche: Fixed finite covariate and ordered-outcome supports make every relevant face and gradient explicit, while still permitting the economically important configurations that defeat smooth delta-method inference.
project_justification.fill: Taking the completed exact-capacity and closed-endpoint mapping as fixed, a finite pathwise secant envelope reduces its sampling problem to a common finite Gaussian maximum. Explicit count-based totalization makes the procedure a well-defined map on every sample, while the uniform empty-cell bound shows that this convention is asymptotically invisible. Near-face retention then delivers honest whole-set coverage and adapts to the oracle on separated configurations.

related_work: The completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem establishes the exact capacities and closed sharp endpoints used here; those identification results are imported rather than claimed as a contribution. Chen and Flores (2015) motivate the always-employed Job Corps complier stratum and bound its mean wage effect, but their inferential discussion excludes bounding functions with nested minimum and maximum operators. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) give ordinary sharp ordinal-benefit bounds, recovered here under perfect compliance and universal selection. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) give sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds, document \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws, and use a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) remedy; the narrower missing result is uniform no-padding coverage of the whole projected survivor-complier quotient interval. Dong and Heiler (2026) derive efficient orthogonal inference for selected-complier mean bounds, but their smooth trimming and relevant-support conditions do not cover discrete ordered atoms or disappearing cell survivor masses. Fang and Santos (2019) explain why ordinary resampling fails for nonlinear directional derivatives and motivate resampling an estimated local derivative. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013), Andrews and Soares (2010), and Andrews and Barwick (2012) motivate retaining near-binding faces. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023) show how localized optimizer sets enter value-function inference. Hsieh, Shi, and Shum (2022) and Cho and Russell (2024) provide optimization-based alternatives, but their procedures do not yield the explicit no-latent-program critical value for this exact whole identified set. Standard multinomial asymptotics are usually written on the event of nonempty conditioning cells; the finite-cell and instrument-overlap conditions here additionally yield an explicit uniform exponential bound for the complement, making all reported empirical and multiplier objects total on finite samples.
technical_internal_limitation: The complete law \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is a boundary stress test, not a theorem that any named published implementation undercovers. Numerical experiments with empirical optimizer-only and survivor-positive screening indicate sensitivity to discarded projection, cut, survivor-minimum, mass-cap, and denominator directions, but no published procedure has been verified to use exactly that composite shortcut. Accordingly no strict single-face undercoverage probability is claimed. Finite multiplier simulation error is also outside the exact-conditional-quantile theorem.
honest_scope: The proposal fixes \(J\) and \(K\), assumes aggregate survivor-complier mass and the nonredundant raw-capacity covariance remain bounded away from zero, and uses the nonnegative-orthant projection. It imposes no lower bound on an individual cell survivor mass, no survivor-gap sign margin, and no cut separation in the main theorem. The exact capacity and closed sharp-endpoint theorem \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) is an established input and is not in the to-prove contribution graph. Every empirical object is defined on all finite samples by the stated denominator fallbacks, and the probability that any such fallback is activated vanishes uniformly. The open contribution is uniform no-padding whole-set inference for the imported mapping; the smooth unique-face and perfect-compliance reductions are proposed corollaries, and the finite atom array is a methodological stress test rather than an undercoverage claim. Automatic data-driven face retention is open. Continuous covariates, weak aggregate denominators, and simulated-quantile error are outside scope.

literature_map.identification: The completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem establishes the exact selected-complier capacities and closed sharp endpoints used as input. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta derive sharp ordinal probability-of-benefit bounds from treatment-arm marginals, and the imported capacity formulas recover those bounds under perfect compliance and universal selection. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen extend symbolic bounds to confounded and imperfect-randomization settings, study \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws, and use a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) remedy. Chen and Flores identify and bound mean wage effects for always-employed Job Corps compliers. The remaining target is inference for the imported survivor-complier quotient mapping.
literature_map.nonsmooth_inference: Fang and Santos characterize failure of the ordinary bootstrap at nonlinear directional derivatives and resample an estimated derivative. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen select near-binding inequalities for intersection bounds. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker localize argmax sets for optimized value functions. These results motivate face retention but do not deliver a signed secant envelope for two projected linear-fractional endpoints with changing support.
literature_map.selected_outcome_inference: Dong and Heiler obtain efficient orthogonal root-\(n\) inference for selected-complier mean bounds under smooth trimming and strong overlap. Their no-point-mass, margin, and relevant-support conditions exclude the discrete atom and vanishing cell-survivor configurations that drive the proposed theorem.
literature_map.optimization_comparators: Hsieh, Shi, and Shum use KKT moment conditions for estimators defined by programs. Cho and Russell perturb linear programs and obtain uniform coverage of an outer set. The proposed computation instead evaluates explicit finite min-cut gradients and targets root-\(n\) coverage of the exact sharp interval without latent optimization or nonvanishing perturbation.
literature_map.novelty_result: No closer paper found in the bounded search subsumes uniform, no-padding, whole-interval multiplier coverage for the explicit survivor-complier benefit map under simultaneous ties and changing cell support. The generic ingredients are published; the new theorem-level work is their nontrivial composition through an unconditional-capacity quotient. The complete finite atom array is a legality and sensitivity diagnostic, not a separate failure claim.

novelty_justification: The exact selected-complier capacity and closed sharp-endpoint mapping is supplied by the completed \(\texttt{pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport}\) theorem and is not a new claim here. The closest published ordinal-inference paper is Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024), which supplies symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds, documents ordinary \(n\)-out-of-\(n\) bootstrap undercoverage at boundary laws, and uses a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) repair; it does not prove uniform no-padding whole-set coverage for the projected survivor-complier quotient. The closest general inference paper is Fang and Santos (2019), which supplies directional-derivative resampling at a fixed map and generic bootstrap-failure diagnostics; it does not prove finite secant domination for a drifting collection of quotient faces or whole-identified-set coverage. Dong and Heiler (2026) obtain efficient normal inference for smooth selected-complier mean bounds, but their trimming regularity and relevant-support overlap exclude ordered atoms and cell survivor masses converging to zero. The strict delta is the common-multiplier finite-face theorem conditional on the imported exact mapping; the atom-table experiment only verifies that the main class genuinely contains simultaneous ties and changing support with nondegenerate covariance.
